articles.what: Teal Vortex gradient blend Up close: One large two-armed spiral with the centre left of middle, drawn as bands 20-25 px wide that alternate emerald, teal, aqua and olive green, with thin slate-blue lines. Every band is hatched with fine diagonal lines and has a few faint pale sparkle points. From a distance: Reads as a green and teal hypnotic spiral or swirl, like a lollipop or pond ripple; the hatching blurs into a soft sheen. Measured spec (average): metal 116, roughness 116, coat 123. Shine: satin. Metal: medium. It brings its own colours.
when: Best on: body, roof, hero panel.
Fits: gt / sports car, show car, stock car.
how: Click the zone you want to change.
Click the BASE MATERIAL box (it says "Click to choose a base") and type "Teal Vortex" in the SEARCH FINISHES box.
Click it to open the big preview, then click Apply.
Leave BASE COLOR on Use finish's own color to keep its colours.
Render and judge it on the car, not on the swatch.
tips: Hood or roof: the single spiral centre becomes a focal point
Side panels: a large tilted section of the swirl, check the centre position
Bands are mid-contrast; white numbers on a dark plate hold, green ones vanish.
Almost nothing: one big spiral is the whole design
Pairs well with: black, white numbers, chrome, silver.
pitfalls: Not concentric rings: the old card says rings from the centre, the render is a spiral
Not a tiling pattern: it is a single large spiral with one centre, so where it lands depends on the panel
Avoid: busy logos over the rings, small numbers over the pattern.
articles.spec_character: Average spec: metal 116 (pearl-level metal), roughness 116 (satin or eggshell), clearcoat 123 (satin or weak clearcoat). The spec is textured, not flat: metal and roughness and clearcoat vary by 20 or more across the surface.
articles.intent_note: Full-finish shelf: the finish carries both its own paint look and its own shine.
articles.paint_advice: It brings its own colours, so leave BASE COLOR on the finish's own colour. Put it next to a plain zone of the opposite sheen (matte beside gloss, warm beside cool) so the colours have a calm neighbour. Avoid: busy logos over the rings, small numbers over the pattern.

combos.why: Patterns that suit it: almost nothing: one big spiral is the whole design; a plain stripe or plate for numbers
Patterns to avoid: other swirl, circle or stripe patterns; fine glitter overlays
Spec overlays that work: gloss clearcoat to saturate the green; none else
Judge the paint and the shine together: the same spec looks different under different colours.

From a distance: A loud acid green and yellow body with orange ribbon edges, like a heat-vision or toxic ooze map; combing disappears, the vertical wavy flow stays. Over it lies a very fine 45-degree diagonal hatch, 2 to 3 px, like twill or scan lines, plus a few tiny pale-blue sparkle specks. From a distance: Reads as a saturated purple-blue gradient, magenta at one end fading to deep blue; the hatch becomes a slight sandy shimmer.
